statements.claim: Yasoda churned curd dressed in a cord-bound cloth, jasmine garland slipping from her hair, face sweating, earrings and bangles swinging with the strain
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.2 (kṣaumaṃ vāsaḥ ... sūtra-naddhaṃ ... vigalan-mālatī ... svinnaṃ vaktraṃ ... kaṅkaṇau kuṇḍale)

statements.claim: The hungry child came to his churning mother
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.3 (stanya-kāma ... mathnantīṃ jananīṃ)

statements.claim: She nursed him on her lap, smiling at his face
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.4 (aṅkam ārūḍham apāyayat stanaṃ ... sa-smitam īkṣatī mukham)

statements.claim: The milk set to boil began to spill, so she set the child down and ran to it
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.6 only says she 'took down the well-cooked milk' (suśṛtaṃ payaḥ); the spilling detail is connective

statements.claim: Angry and biting his lip, the child broke the churn-pot
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.5 (sañjāta-kopaḥ ... sandaśya dadbhir dadhi-mantha-bhājanam)

statements.claim: He gave the stolen butter to a monkey
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.7 (markāya kāmaṃ dadataṃ)

statements.claim: He stood on the mortar
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.7 (ulūkhalāṅghrer upari vyavasthitaṃ)

statements.claim: Yasoda saw the broken pot, took a stick, and chased him; he ran as if afraid
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.8 (ātta-yaṣṭiṃ ... apasasāra bhītavat)

statements.claim: The yogis' minds cannot reach or enter him
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.8 (na yam āpa yogināṃ kṣamaṃ praveṣṭuṃ tapaseritaṃ manaḥ)

statements.claim: Yasoda, broad-hipped and slender-waisted, could not catch him
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.9 (bṛhac-calac-chroṇī-bharākrānta-gatiḥ sumadhyamā)

statements.claim: He cried, rubbing his eyes with hands smeared with collyrium and soot
statements.evidence: BP 10.9.10 (prarudantam akṣiṇī kaṣantam añjan-maṣiṇī sva-pāṇinā)

notes: Faithful to BP 10.9.1-10. Only connective narration is the boiling-milk spill (source says 'took down the cooked milk'). Uses 'Yasoda' (pack index spelling) consistently.

statements.claim: Krishna was a crawling child, too young to walk
statements.evidence: HV 1.62 'began to crawl on their legs'; BP 10.10 context (bālena)

statements.claim: He went into cow sheds covered in ash and dung, and pasted in ashes and cow-dung shone like a prince of fire
statements.evidence: HV 1.62 'with their persons pasted with ashes and powdered cow-dung they shone like two princes of fire' (note: HV says 'two boys'; story singularizes to Krishna, matching BP primary which is Krishna-only)

statements.claim: Nanda could not check him
statements.evidence: HV 1.62 'Nanda could not (by any means) check them'

statements.claim: In anger Yashoda tied a rope around his waist to a wooden mortar
statements.evidence: HV 1.62; VP 5.6 'Fastening a cord round his waist, she tied him to the wooden mortar'

statements.claim: She told him 'Go, if you are capable of it'
statements.evidence: HV 1.62 'Go, if you are capable of doing it' (paraphrase)

statements.claim: From that rope he was called Damodara, bound by a rope around his belly
statements.evidence: HV 1.62 'From that day ... Krishna was called Damodara'; VP 5.6 'hence ... called Damodara'

statements.claim: He dragged the mortar toward the forest edge where two twin arjuna trees stood
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.25 (arjunayoḥ ... yamayor); HV 1.62

statements.claim: He went meaning to surprise the villagers and play
statements.evidence: HV 1.62 'with a view to surprise the inhabitants of Vraja and play'

statements.claim: The mortar caught at the roots and a single tug uprooted both trees
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.26; HV 1.62 'mortar firmly fixed at the root ... uprooted with their roots and branches'; VP 5.6

statements.claim: Birds burst from the branches and dust rose
statements.evidence: Connective atmosphere, not in the cited verses

statements.claim: The two trees were sons of Kubera, cursed by a divine sage to stand rooted until freed
statements.evidence: BP 10.10.24 (dhanadātmajau = two sons of Kubera; devarṣi = the divine sage)

statements.claim: The cowherds came running and Krishna laughed
statements.evidence: HV 1.62 'to show this to the milk-men the Lord ... began to laugh'

notes: Primary (BP 10.10.23-26) is Krishna-only; ash/dung 'prince of fire' color drawn from HV (additional). HV/VP both fold in the rope-binding beat, matching the story. Clean.

statements.claim: Aghasura was a demon in the shape of an immense python
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.35 (ājagaraṃ carma — the python's skin)

statements.claim: The cowherd boys and calves had gone into his open mouth, alive but not yet swallowed
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.25 (praviṣṭās tv asurodarāntaraṃ ... na gīrṇāḥ)

statements.claim: Krishna was pierced with pity and amazed at what fate had done
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.26 (ghṛṇārdito ... diṣṭa-kṛtena vismitaḥ)

statements.claim: He reasoned about the demon's life and the boys' harm, then entered the mouth
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.27 (kṛtyaṃ kim atrāsya khalasya jīvanaṃ ... jñātvāviśat tuṇḍam)

statements.claim: The gods hidden in the clouds cried out in fear
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.28 (ghana-cchadā devā bhayād dhā-heti cukruśuḥ)

statements.claim: Krishna grew, blocking the demon's throat; its eyes bulged and it thrashed
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.29-30 (niruddha-mārgiṇaḥ ... udgīrṇa-dṛṣṭer bhramatas)

statements.claim: As the demon's life left, Krishna raised up the dead boys and calves and led them out alive
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.31 (vatsān suhṛdaḥ paretān — the dead companions)

statements.claim: A great light rose from the demon, blazing the ten directions, and entered Krishna
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.32 (mahaj jyotiḥ ... jvalayad diśo daśa); pack summary 'soul merges into Krishna'

statements.claim: Gods rained flowers, gandharvas sang, apsaras danced, brahmins raised hymns
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.33 (puṣpaiḥ ... apsarasaś ca nartanaiḥ gītaiḥ ... stavaiś ca viprā)

statements.claim: Only the dried skin remained in Vrindavan
statements.evidence: BP 10.12.35 (ājagaraṃ carma śuṣkaṃ vṛndāvane 'dbhutam)

notes: Faithful to BP 10.12.25-35. The 'second moon / sun at night' is a connective simile over v.32, not a factual claim. Correctly distinguishes 'not yet swallowed' (alive) from later death-and-revival (paretān).

statements.claim: The calves and cowherd boys of Vrindavan vanished
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt 'every vanished calf and boy'; BP 10.13.17-26

statements.claim: Mothers waited in doorways and cows lowed for their calves
statements.evidence: Connective scene-setting; implied by BP 10.13.17 (to give joy to the mothers)

statements.claim: Krishna expanded himself into every vanished calf and boy to console their mothers
statements.evidence: BP 10.13.17 (mudaṃ kartuṃ tan-mātṝṇāṃ); pack summary

statements.claim: He took on each one's body, staff, horn, flute, leaf, ornaments, clothes, temperament, name, age, and play
statements.evidence: BP 10.13.18 (yaṣṭi-viṣāṇa-veṇu-dala ... vibhūṣāmbaram ... śīla-guṇābhidhākṛti-vayo ... vihāra)

statements.claim: Each boy led his own calf to its own pen
statements.evidence: BP 10.13.20 (tat-tad-vatsān pṛthaṅ nītvā tat-tad-goṣṭhe niveśya)

statements.claim: Cows hurried lowing to their calves; mothers rose at the flute, embraced, bathed, dressed, marked tilak and fed them
statements.evidence: BP 10.13.21-23 (veṇu-rava-tvarotthitā ... tilakāśanādibhiḥ)

statements.claim: The cows' and mothers' love grew deeper than before
statements.evidence: BP 10.13.24 (go-gopīnāṃ mātṛtā ... snehardhikāṃ)

statements.claim: This lasted a full year, affection climbing daily like a vine
statements.evidence: BP 10.13.25 (sneha-vally ābdam anvaham)

statements.claim: None of the mothers or cows knew it was Krishna
statements.evidence: Pack summary 'unknowingly nurses and loves the Lord himself'

notes: Very high fidelity to BP 10.13.17-26; the enumeration of boy attributes tracks v.18 almost item-for-item. The 'gentler way' framing is connective over the 'give joy to mothers' motive.

statements.claim: A wildfire suddenly surrounded the cowherd boys and their cattle in the dry woods
statements.evidence: Pack summary and BP 10.19 excerpt (agnim ulbaṇam — the raging fire)

statements.claim: The fire came from every side at once
statements.evidence: Source does not specify direction; connective elaboration

statements.claim: The boys cried out that Krishna's own kinsmen did not deserve to perish
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.9 (nūnaṃ tvad-bāndhavāḥ kṛṣṇa na cārhanty avasāditum)

statements.claim: Krishna told them not to fear and to shut their eyes
statements.evidence: Pack summary 'bids ... close their eyes'; BP 10.19.11 (mīlitākṣeṣu)

statements.claim: He drank the raging fire into his mouth until it was gone
statements.evidence: Pack summary 'drinks up the flames'; BP 10.19.11

statements.claim: They opened their eyes and stood safe at Bhandira with their cattle unhurt
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.12 (akṣīṇy unmīlya punar bhāṇḍīram āpitāḥ)

statements.claim: It was his yogic power, accomplished by his own maya
statements.evidence: BP 10.19.13 (kṛṣṇasya yoga-vīryaṃ tad yoga-māyānubhāvitam)

statements.claim: Later they tried to tell the elders, who smiled and let it go
statements.evidence: Invented epilogue, not in the source; narrative closure only

notes: No unsupported facts; core event fully sourced. Flagged items are connective: the 'from every side' direction and the invented elders-epilogue are narration beyond BP 10.19.9-13.

statements.claim: Kaliya coiled around Krishna and squeezed while the people of Gokula (women and children) watched helpless, grieving on his account
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.22 (sva-gokulam ... sa-strī-kumāram ati-duḥkhitam ātma-hetoḥ)

statements.claim: Following the path of a mortal, Krishna paused a moment and rose from the coils
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.22 (ājñāya martya-padavīm anuvartamānaḥ sthitvā muhūrtam udatiṣṭhad)

statements.claim: Kaliya rose in fury, spread his hundred hoods, hissed, eyes like burning coals, forked tongue, poison-fire glance
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.23-24 (unmamayya kupitaḥ sva-phaṇān ... ulmuka-mukho ... jihvayā dvi-śikhayā ... viṣāgni-dṛṣṭim)

statements.claim: Krishna circled him like the king of birds (Garuda)
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.24 (parisasāra yathā khagendro)

statements.claim: The serpent's strength ebbed from circling
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.25 (paribhrama-hataujasam)

statements.claim: Krishna climbed onto the hoods and danced; the rubies reddened his feet
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.25 (adhirūḍha ... nanarta; mūrdha-ratna-nikara-sparśāti-tāmra-pādāmbuja)

statements.claim: Each hood that would not bow he crushed with his foot; the serpent vomited blood
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.27-28 (yad yac chiro na namate ... mamarda; āsyato 'sṛṅ ... vaman)

statements.claim: Gandharvas, siddhas, sages and wives of the gods showered flowers, music and praise
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.26 (gandharva-siddha-muni-cāraṇa-deva-vadhvaḥ ... puṣpopahāra-nutibhiḥ)

statements.claim: Kaliya remembered Narayana, guru of all moving and still, and took refuge in him
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.29 (carācara-guruṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tam araṇaṃ manasā jagāma)

statements.claim: The serpent's wives approached in grief, garments and ornaments loosened
statements.evidence: BP 10.16.30 (amuṣya patnya ārtāḥ ślathad-vasana-bhūṣaṇa-keśa-bandhāḥ)

notes: Faithful to BP 10.16.22-30; the 'hundred heads', 'rubies', 'king of birds', and the Narayana refuge all track the verses closely. No fabrication.

statements.claim: Out-of-season rain fell in sheets with hail like stones and wind; cattle trembled and cowherds cried 'Krishna! Krishna!'
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.10-12 (aty-āsārāti-vātena paśavo jāta-vepanāḥ ... kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa)

statements.claim: This was Indra, king of the gods, angry
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt 'Krishna reasoned that Indra in anger was sending this out-of-season storm'

statements.claim: The cowherds had always kept a sacrifice to Indra; that year at Krishna's urging the cowherd king offered a different sacrifice (of the cows) and Indra's offering was not made
statements.evidence: Backstory bridge; BP 3.2.31 gives go-savena (go-savana sacrifice) and bhagnamāne (Indra's pride broken) but not the 'always worshiped Indra' premise

statements.claim: Krishna resolved to shelter his people and break the pride of those who fancy themselves lords
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt 'to destroy the pride of those who fancy themselves lords'

statements.claim: He lifted Govardhana hill with one hand, lightly, like an umbrella, as if on the tip of his finger
statements.evidence: BP 10.25.18 (ekena hastena kṛtvā govardhanācalam); HV 1.73 'on the tip of his finger'; pack summary 'like an umbrella'

statements.claim: The storm lasted seven days and seven nights
statements.evidence: VP 5.11 'For seven days and nights ... rain upon the Gokula'; pack variant_notes 'HV/VP specify seven nights/days'

statements.claim: The people and cattle stayed dry beneath the raised hill
statements.evidence: VP 5.11 'they were protected by the elevation of the mountain'

statements.claim: On the seventh day the storm broke and Indra's pride was broken
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.32 (varṣatīndre vrajaḥ kopād bhagnamāne)

notes: Core event fully sourced. The Indra-worship backstory ('always kept a sacrifice to Indra ... the offering was not made') is a connective bridge — the go-savana and Indra's broken pride are in BP 3.2.31-32, but the 'annual Indra sacrifice' premise is not explicit in the pack. No fabrication.

statements.claim: The full moon rose, washing the eastern sky red like fresh kumkum
statements.evidence: BP 10.29.1-2 (uḍurājaḥ ... prācyā ... aruṇena; nava-kuṅkumāruṇam)

statements.claim: On an autumn night Krishna saw the forest and played his flute / sang sweetly
statements.evidence: BP 10.29.2 (dṛṣṭvā ... vanaṃ ... jagau kalaṃ); pack index 'autumn night'

statements.claim: The women of Vraja heard it and their minds were seized by Krishna
statements.evidence: BP 10.29.3 (vraja-striyaḥ kṛṣṇa-gṛhīta-mānasāḥ)

statements.claim: One left milking, one left serving food, one left feeding milk to an infant, one left anointing, one left collyrium half applied to her eyes
statements.evidence: BP 10.29.4-6 (duhantyo ... dohaṃ hitvā; pariveṣayantyas; pāyayantyaḥ śiśūn payaḥ; limpantyaḥ; añjantyaḥ locane)

statements.claim: Husbands, fathers, brothers and kinsmen tried to restrain them
statements.evidence: BP 10.29.7 (vāryamāṇāḥ patibhiḥ pitṛbhir bhrātṛ-bandhubhiḥ)

statements.claim: Some could not get out of their houses and, through the fierce pain of separation, were united with him (attained him with eyes shut)
statements.evidence: BP 10.29.8-10 (antar-gṛha-gatāḥ ... 'labdha-vinirgamāḥ; duḥsaha-preṣṭha-viraha-tīvra-tāpa ... tam eva paramātmānaṃ ... saṅgatāḥ)

statements.claim: Krishna saw the women of Vraja come near
statements.evidence: BP 10.29.16 (tā dṛṣṭvāntikam āyātā bhagavān vraja-yoṣitaḥ)

notes: Faithful to BP 10.29.1-16; the five abandoned tasks track vv.4-6 exactly. The 'shut their eyes' rendering of the house-bound gopis' mystical union is a reasonable paraphrase of vv.8-10.
